runs.note: The reading run's product crops against the round-3 artboards and specs copied from that run's artifact (UX-P5.fix-1 DO 4-5). No finding on the severity pill, the placeholder's copy or the gear. Every standing and single-judge finding is the artboard lagging the product's ruled form: accepted-as-design under follow-up 1 and routed to one artboard row. The single-judge main-installed-all#D1 is a major and carries its disposition (follow-up 1, DO NOT).

refuted.finding: The NETStandard.Library row's Props pill starts 4 px after the SDK pill in the capture (SDK 259–293, Props from 298), while the approved artboard draws it 8 px after (Props from 302). The capture satisfies DS-ROW-1, which sets 4 px between consecutive pills; the artboard is what departs from the rule, so this is a drawing conflict and not a CSS defect.
refuted.reason: The crop shows the SDK pill at x 259-293 in both images, with Props starting at x 298 in the capture and at x 302 on the artboard. The capture is the side that is right: the hard measurement 'DS-ROW-1@main-transitive-details: ... badges: name gap 8 ×2, pill gap 4 (hard)' matches DS-ROW-1's 4 px between pills, so the product has no defect and the 8 px gap is a drawing error in the artboard, which spec.json does not declare.

findings.finding: [native] The details facts block (Version to Report abuse) keeps a 24–25 px row pitch in the capture, as DS-ALIGN-2 requires (6 px apart, pitch at least 24). The artboard draws the same rows at a 22–23 px pitch, so in the capture the block, and the Vulnerabilities and Dependencies blocks below it, sit about 10 px lower than in the artboard. The artboard disagrees with the rule. | [geometry] The details pane's facts rows (Version to Report abuse) sit at a 24 px pitch in the capture (line tops 295, 320, 344, 368, 392, 416, 441), as DS-ALIGN-2 requires (6 px apart, pitch at least 24), while the approved artboard draws the same rows at about 22 px (295, 318, 342, 364, 386, 408, 431), so everything below them in the artboard sits 10 px higher; the rule wins and the capture is right, but the artboard drawing disagrees with it.
